subject: biology
title: Efficiency of biomass transfer (Separate science)
key_idea: Only about 10% of the biomass at one trophic level is transferred to the next. The rest is lost, so less is available at each step. This is why food chains have only a few trophic levels.

blocks.text: (Separate science) Efficiency compares what is passed on with what was available. This section covers how to calculate it.

blocks.label: Percentage efficiency of transfer
blocks.formula: percentage efficiency = (energy or biomass in the next level ÷ energy or biomass in the previous level) × 100
where: energy in kJ, or biomass in g/m² or kg, in the next level
energy or biomass in the previous level, in the same unit

blocks.label: Percentage lost
blocks.formula: percentage lost = ((previous level − next level) ÷ previous level) × 100
where: previous level and next level, in the same unit

items.text: In a river food chain the biomass is: algae 840, invertebrate animals 200, small fish 40, large fish 10 (all in g/m²).
From invertebrate animals to small fish: 40 ÷ 200 × 100 = 20%.
From algae to large fish: (840 − 10) ÷ 840 × 100 = 98.8%. To 2 significant figures this is 99%.

blocks.text: Give your answer to the number of significant figures the question asks for.

diagram.alt: Practise calculating the percentage efficiency of an energy transfer between two trophic levels. The numbers change each time.
diagram.question: The producers in an ecosystem contain **{I} kJ** of energy. The primary consumers contain **{O} kJ**. Calculate the percentage efficiency of the energy transfer from the producers to the primary consumers.
working: Percentage efficiency = (energy in the next level ÷ energy in the previous level) × 100

items: Percentage efficiency = next level ÷ previous level × 100.
Use the same unit for both levels, and round as the question asks.

blocks.text: Typically only about 10% of the biomass is passed on. This section covers why the rest is lost.

items: Not all of an organism is eaten, for example bones and shells.
Not all of what is eaten is digested and absorbed. Some is egested.
Respiration breaks down glucose to release energy for movement and keeping warm. The energy is lost as heat, and carbon is lost as carbon dioxide.
Excretion removes waste such as urea and carbon dioxide.
Dead material is broken down by decomposers.

blocks.text: Mammals and birds keep a constant body temperature, so they lose more heat. Their transfers are less efficient.

items: About 90% of the biomass is lost at each transfer.
Losses are uneaten parts, egestion, excretion and respiration.

blocks.text: Biomass is lost at every step. This section covers what that means for the length of a food chain.

items: Each trophic level has only about 10% of the biomass of the level below.
After a few steps there is too little biomass left to support another level.
So food chains usually have only four or five trophic levels.

diagram.alt: Change the biomass in the producers and the percentage transferred, and see how much biomass is left at trophic levels 2, 3 and 4.

inputs.label: Percentage transferred to the next level

items: Biomass falls at each trophic level, so there is little left after a few steps.
This limits the number of trophic levels in a food chain.

checks.q: A caterpillar-eating bird gets 8 kJ from the 100 kJ of energy in its food. Calculate the percentage efficiency of the transfer.
Give two reasons why only some of the biomass of an animal's food becomes the biomass of the animal.
checks.a: Any two from: not all of the food is eaten, not all is digested (egested), respiration, excretion.

checks.q: Explain why food chains rarely have more than five trophic levels.
checks.a: Biomass is lost at each transfer, so only about 10% passes on. By the fifth level there is too little biomass left to support another level.

exam_phrases: respiration or respiring
excretion (by the animal)
non-eaten parts
egestion / faeces
not all parts are absorbed / digested
carbon dioxide from respiration
urea from excretion
less energy lost as heat
less energy lost in movement

mistakes.wrong: Respiration produces energy, so energy is lost.
mistakes.right: "Respiration produces / makes / creates energy" is not accepted. Say that biomass is lost as carbon dioxide from respiration, or that energy is lost as heat or in movement.

mistakes.wrong: Cows reared indoors are more efficient because less energy is lost.
mistakes.right: "Less energy lost" on its own is ignored. Say less energy is lost as heat, and less energy is lost in movement.

mistakes.wrong: Some of the insects' biomass is lost as energy.
mistakes.right: References to loss of energy are ignored when the question asks about biomass. Name what is lost: carbon dioxide from respiration, urea from excretion, or parts not absorbed or digested.

mistakes.wrong: The percentage of biomass lost is 98.81%.
mistakes.right: Round as the question asks. To 2 significant figures the answer is 99%.

worked_example.question:
A food chain for organisms in a river has four trophic levels. The biomass at each level is: algae 840 g/m², invertebrate animals 200 g/m², small fish 40 g/m², large fish 10 g/m².

Calculate the percentage of the biomass lost between the algae and the large fish.

Give your answer to 2 significant figures.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the calculation, one for the unrounded value and one for rounding to 2 significant figures. An answer of 99 scores all 3 marks.

blocks.text: Farmers can raise efficiency by reducing the energy their animals lose.

items: Rearing cows indoors is more efficient because less energy is lost as heat and less is lost in movement.
Disadvantages of rearing indoors: disease spreads more easily, so more antibiotics are used, and heating, lighting, food and drugs cost more.
Aggressive behaviour and stress can reduce productivity.

blocks.text: A ratio compares two biomass values in their simplest form.

items.text: A farmer's maize seeds have a biomass of 4200 kg. The chickens fed on them have a total biomass of 2200 kg.

exam_phrases: not all the mass of the leaves is transferred to the snails
some of the leaves were not digested / absorbed
some of the leaves were excreted / egested
some mass was used up in respiration / providing energy
some mass / energy was used up by the snail moving
leaf mass may be digested by decomposers

mistakes.wrong: The energy transferred to the chipmunks is 9 262.5 kJ.
mistakes.right: Give the answer to the nearest whole number as asked: 9 263 kJ.

mistakes.wrong: The caterpillar's mass went up by 1.5 g, so it ate 1.5 g of nettles.
mistakes.right: The 1.5 g gain is only 10% of the food eaten. Multiply by 10: 1.5 × 10 = 15 g.

mistakes.wrong: All of the mass the leaves lose becomes extra mass of the snails.
mistakes.right: The snails gain less than the leaves lose. Explain why: some leaf was not digested or was egested or excreted, some was used in respiration or movement, and decomposers may break some down.

worked_example.question:
Siberian chipmunks eat acorns, which are the seeds of oak trees.

The percentage of energy transferred from the acorns to the chipmunks is 9.5%.
The energy contained in the acorns is 97 500 kJ.
Calculate the amount of energy transferred to the chipmunks.
Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
answer_points: To the nearest whole number: 9 263 kJ.
worked_example.tip: Full marks for the correct answer with no working. Alternatively 97 500 × 0.095 = 9 262.5 kJ.

blocks.text: Sometimes the percentage and the amount transferred are given, and you find the amount eaten.

items.text: A caterpillar's mass rises from 6.0 g to 7.5 g, a gain of 1.5 g.
It converts 10% of its food into body mass, so it ate 1.5 × 10 = 15 g of nettles.

exam_phrases: insecticides will kill insect pests
less leaves will be eaten
more food / glucose / biomass made by photosynthesis
more plant growth / food / biomass for cattle
more biomass passes through the agricultural food chain
cattle receive more energy for growth

mistakes.wrong: GM plants that make insecticide have more biomass because they kill insects.
mistakes.right: Link the ideas. The insecticide kills pests, so fewer leaves are eaten and there is more photosynthesis. So more biomass passes along the food chain to the cattle and then to humans.

mistakes.wrong: The GM plants photosynthesise more, so there is more biomass.
mistakes.right: Explain with both photosynthesis and the function of the insecticide, and link them to the food chain, to reach the top level.
